statement.p: Sketch the region of integration and evaluate by changing to polar coordinates:

static.solution:
0\le x\le \frac{1}{2},\quad \sqrt{3}x\le y\le \sqrt{1-{x}^2} \mathcal{D} is the circular sector shown in the figure.
The ray y=\sqrt{3}x in the first quadrant has the polar equation r \sin \theta =\sqrt{3}r \cos \theta \quad\Rightarrow\quad \tan \theta =\sqrt{3}\quad\Rightarrow\quad \theta =\frac{\pi }{3} Therefore, \mathcal{D} lies in the angular sector \frac{\pi }{3}\le \theta \le \frac{\pi }{2}. Also, the circle y=\sqrt{1-{x}^2} has the polar equation r=1, hence \mathcal{D} can be described by the inequalities \frac{\pi }{3}\le \theta \le \frac{\pi }{2},\quad 0\le r\le 1 We use change of variables to obtain \int_0^{1/2} \int_{\sqrt{3}x}^{\sqrt{1-{x}^2}} 24 x \,dy \,dx= \int_{\pi/3}^{\pi/2} \int_0^1 24 r( \cos \theta )r \,dr \,d\theta= \int_{\pi/3}^{\pi/2} \int_0^1 24 {r}^2 \cos \theta \,dr \,d\theta=\int_{\pi/3}^{\pi/2} 24\cdot\frac{{r}^3 \cos \theta }{3}\bigg|_{r=0}^1 \,d\theta= \int_{\pi/3}^{\pi/2} 8\cos\theta\,d\theta= 8\sin \theta\bigg|_{\pi/3}^{\pi/2}=8\left( \sin \frac{\pi }{2}- \sin \frac{\pi}{3}\right)= 8\left(1-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) \approx 1.0718
